$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Security Hub + GuardDuty (core/secscan_core.py). See s3.json for the contract.

securityhub.findings.title: Security Hub: EnableSecurityHub, GetFindings (filters, sort, paging), BatchUpdateFindings workflow, ASFF documents
limitations: Findings are derived live from the simulated resources by Vyomi's own rules (AWS Foundational Security Best Practices controls S3.2, S3.4, S3.8, EC2.9, EC2.13, EC2.14, RDS.2, RDS.3, IAM.5, CloudTrail.1) - a small subset of the FSBP catalogue, no CIS/PCI standards, no cross-Region aggregation, no custom insights or automation rules. Inspector-style findings: network reachability of instances (public IP + world-open security group), end-of-life Lambda runtimes, and CVE findings for scanned images. GuardDuty findings flow into Security Hub once a detector exists. Filters supported: SeverityLabel, ProductName, Title, ResourceType, ResourceId, ComplianceStatus, WorkflowStatus, RecordState, GeneratorId, Id, ProductArn.

securityhub.home.title: Console Home: Security widget (live counts by severity)

guardduty.detector.title: GuardDuty: detectors, ListFindings/GetFindings, archive, CreateSampleFindings
limitations: There is no real attacker, VPC flow, DNS or CloudTrail-event stream: findings come from a DETERMINISTIC rule engine over the control-plane calls the simulator served (CloudTrail stopped, bucket opened to anonymous access, administrator policy attached, credentials minted in a burst, repeated denials, enumeration bursts). Finding types reuse GuardDuty names where an equivalent exists; every finding carries detector=vyomi-rules. No machine-learning anomaly detection, EBS/EC2 malware scanning, runtime monitoring, S3/EKS/RDS protection plans or multi-account administration. CreateSampleFindings creates clearly labelled [SAMPLE] findings. Only calls served through the simulator's own wire are observed (EC2 security-group changes on the offline appliance are covered by the posture rules instead).
